answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed if its actions are proven fraudulent, and earn reputation only through interactions with independently bonded agents. Creating a thousand identities then requires a thousand funded bonds; splitting a fixed stake across them makes each easier to slash and gives each little influence. A dune of fresh accounts cannot cheaply inherit the track record of a cedar-rooted participant, while a vine of reciprocal fake reviews is detectable when the bonded counterparties share control. The attacker pays capital and risks losing it for every identity.
